beats.text: This is Kalwings, live. Freshers struggle to show what they can do, and employers struggle to see it. In three minutes, watch a student prove a skill by completing a real challenge, and an employer review that proof.
Meet a final-year student. She signs in and opens Challenges: real tasks set by employers, open to everyone.
Every card shows who is hiring and what the task is. Pay or reward, location and eligibility are always shown up front, so there are no surprises.

The brief is a real task, not a quiz. And the rubric shows exactly how a person will judge her work: forty points for correctness, thirty for clarity, and thirty for the write-up. She knows the rules before she starts.
She builds her solution, then submits a title, a short write-up of her approach, and a link to her work.
One click to submit. It is saved, and she can update it until it has been reviewed.
It now appears in her submissions, waiting for a person to read it.
A recruiter at Sample Co A opens Challenges and sees every submission, one per candidate.
Instead of a CV, the recruiter sees the actual work: the write-up, and the link. Nothing is hidden behind a score.
She opens Review and scores each rubric criterion, in points, against what the candidate really delivered.
She adds written feedback, chooses an outcome, and awards the skill, so it is backed by evidence.
A person makes every decision. There is no automatic rejection, and scores are advice, not a verdict.
Saved. The candidate is shortlisted, and joins the employer's hiring pipeline.
Later, when she searches talent by skill, verified evidence is shown separately from self-declared skills. So the recruiter always knows which claims were proven, and which were only stated.
Back to the student. She sees her score and the feedback straight away.
And the skill the employer awarded now appears on her public profile, with the reason it was awarded. That is proof anyone can check.
Students get a fair way to show real work. Employers see proof, not promises. And every decision stays with a person.
Real work, judged by people. That is Kalwings.
